evidence: Clear separation into logical layers: 'models' (data/domain), 'services' (business logic orchestration), 'utils' (cross-cutting utilities), 'routes' (presentation/controller layer)
Routes depend on services, utils, and models, but not vice versa — unidirectional dependency flow
Services abstract external interactions (HTTP, CSE) with dedicated client classes
Models encapsulate data and configuration without direct knowledge of higher layers
App directory structure mirrors classic layered architecture (presentation → business → data)
Flask app instance in __init__.py coordinates layers, typical of layered designs
Low package count (5) and shallow depth (3) indicate centralized but well-organized layering
risks: High fan-out (avg 4.36) suggests some modules are too aware of many others — could indicate leaking abstraction boundaries
Some utilities (e.g., utils/misc.py) contain diverse functionality — risk of becoming a 'dump' module
Direct import of app in test files may create tight coupling between test and app internals
